items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-10-20
items.q: I was sort of Leon's godfather... we were very close.

ctx.x: You know where Bailey's is? On Brown Street. All right. At one time, the Rosefeld Hotel used to be right, right where it is, except that where they had the, in later years, became the fountain, fountain lounge, and the breakfast room for the, breakfast room or the fountain lounge was where Bailey's is now. In other words, they used to do, when Kellner was there, they used to, on weekends when they'd have a big crowd, he was playing in the fountain, in the fountain room, fountain room lounge, and uh, they would…
Did you play with Kellner, Dan?

I said, I was, I was sort of, I was sort of Leon's godfather. Really? Whenever he needed a substitute, when he went to New York, I'd end up playing piano for him. And, uh, whenever he wanted to fire somebody, he'd have to ask me, how do you fire him? And we were very close. In fact, the last thing he asked me to do is how to, how to get out of, of, uh, get out of, uh, a losing proposition belonging to the New York local. And I told him I've got the same problem that we've been in so long that we pay for our life…
